issues.title: Reapproval
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> Every revision change suspends issuance until an administrator approves the changed entry ([Installation and Reconciliation](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#installation)), even when the change only adds an item that no approval includes ([Example Approval Lifecycle](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#example-lifecycle)). The essential invariant is that no change expands an approval. Whether issuance can continue while the approved subset remains within the changed entry's Authorization Envelope, and what a Resource Authorization Server would publish to make that safe, are open.

The [Example Approval Lifecycle](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#example-lifecycle) appendix shows the operational cost: adding an unrelated optional scope value suspends issuance until an administrator approves the entry again.

issues.title: Token path
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> A catalog access token is issued only in response to a catalog access assertion ([Catalog Access Token Response](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#token-response)). Whether other token requests that establish the same Issuer Relationship with the same guarantees can also obtain one, so that existing authorization infrastructure can be used, is open.

issues.title: Client-specific views for the Grant Issuer
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> A Relationship View is relationship-wide ([Clients](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#clients)). Whether Resource Authorization Servers restrict grant configurations by client often enough to need an optional view, retrieved by the Grant Issuer, for one identified client is open. Such a view would keep two parties distinct: the application client it describes, identified by its client identifier at the Resource Authorization Server, and the Issuer Relationship that retrieves it. The Issuer Relationship would need authorization to inspect that client's configuration; [ID-JAG Section 9.7](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant-06.html#section-9.7) requires client authentication for client-facing discovery. The client context would include the target tenant where needed to identify the client registration ([ID-JAG Section 6.2](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant-06.html#section-6.2)), and the response would identify that context for comparison with the request. Installed state, revision comparisons, and approvals would be scoped to that context, and those approvals would apply only to grants identifying that client. The view would only narrow what the relationship permits.

issues.title: Client-facing discovery
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> An application client retrieving its own view, the protected discovery mechanism that [ID-JAG Section 9.7](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant-06.html#section-9.7) permits, is a different consumer from the Grant Issuer. A design considered for this draft has the client authenticate at a discovery endpoint of the Resource Authorization Server, name the Grant Issuer, issuer tenant, and resource, and receive the Tenant Objects and entries of that Relationship View that it is authorized to learn about, with the same response for unknown and unauthorized contexts. Each Grant Profile would map an entry to request parameters, because members such as a required claim constrain the grant rather than the request. Such a view selects whole entries, so it cannot express a restriction for one client that is narrower than an entry, and the Grant Issuer can issue a grant using a different entry from the one the client used. Whether that contract is useful, and how it relates to the Grant Issuer's approvals, are open.

A full specification was drafted in #8 (endpoint, disclosure rules, client view, ID-JAG request mapping) and deferred from -00 in #11. The text is in the history of #8.

issues.title: Freshness and termination
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> A Grant Issuer stops issuing under state it cannot refresh only after a maximum age that it configures, which is a recommendation ([Installation and Reconciliation](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#installation)), so the Resource Authorization Server has no deadline it can rely on after it ends a relationship ([Stale Catalogs and Relationship Termination](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#sec-stale)). Whether to require a maximum age, or to let the Resource Authorization Server publish one, is open.

Raised by the security review in #10 and recorded as an open issue in #11 instead of adding a mechanism before -00. Options discussed: make the maximum age a MUST; let the Resource Authorization Server publish an upper bound in the Relationship View; or keep the documented procedure (empty the view, wait for the Grant Issuer to observe the withdrawal, then end the relationship).

issues.title: Supporting metadata
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> How a Grant Issuer uses authorization details schemas to enforce policy, including retaining a schema and requiring new approval when it changes; how it matches authority metadata entries to the items of an entry; and how it uses declared attenuation when narrowing a request ([Optional Supporting Metadata](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#optional-metadata)).

The detailed rules were in the draft until #11, which reduced Optional Supporting Metadata to a short note.

issues.title: Registries
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> Whether to establish registries for catalog members and grant binding methods, and with what registration policy, is open; a registry of members would record which members are part of the normative semantics of an entry.

issues.title: Must-understand extensions
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> A mechanism by which an entry marks the extension members that a Grant Issuer must implement to use it, so that restrictive extensions can be defined without a distinct Grant Profile identifier ([Extensibility](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#extensibility)). It is to be added before the format stabilizes, or with the first restrictive extension. A related question is whether every extension is to preserve the principles in [Protocol Overview](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#overview) for a Grant Issuer that does not implement it.

issues.title: Implementation experience
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Listed in the draft's [Open Issues](https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog/draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog.html#open-issues) appendix.

> Evidence that a Resource Authorization Server can generate entries and revisions from the configuration it enforces, and that independent Grant Issuers configure the same integration from one catalog with less manual work.

pulls.title: Add -00 of the OAuth Authorization Grant Catalog
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body: Adds draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog -00 and removes the template placeholder. Open issues are listed in the document.

pulls.title: Consolidate and compress the -00 draft
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Removes restatement so that each rule has one home, and cites dependencies instead of restating them. The draft goes from 77 to 62 pages and from 19,880 to 15,542 source words.

## Structural changes

- **Registries deferred.** The Catalog Members and Grant Binding Methods registries are removed and listed as an open issue. An extension states which of its members count toward an entry's revision. `dpop` and `mtls` are defined where they are used.
- **Retrieval Binding requirements** are folded into Extensibility.
- **JWT section folded into the ID-JAG Grant Profile Definition.** The `typ` guidance for future JWT profiles moves to Grant Profile Definitions. The `jwt-bearer` requirement now applies only when the Resource Authorization Server lists the ID-JAG profile in `authorization_grant_profiles_supported` (ID-JAG Section 7.2).
- **The DPoP-bound catalog access assertion is kept.**

## Requirement changes

- The two rules about using one binding at a time are now lowercase statements in Extensibility.
- The `grant_types_supported` MUST is scoped to the ID-JAG profile.

The compression edits leave the ordered BCP 14 keyword sequence unchanged (143 keywords).

## Delegation

- Errors that RFC 6749, RFC 6750, and JWT-DPOP already assign now cite those specifications. The error mappings this draft adds are kept, as are its 401 and 403 status codes.
- Security and Privacy subsections are reduced to the threat, the rule that mitigates it, and the residual risk.
- RFC 8126 is removed from the references.

## Checks

- Builds at 62 pages.
- idnits: only template indentation warnings and the two draft downrefs (ID-JAG, JWT-DPOP).
- All references are cited and every citation resolves.

pulls.title: Fix consistency issues left by the consolidation pass
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Fixes nine issues that a cold consistency read found after #2. Each fix is a separate commit. No requirement keywords change; there are still 143.

## Corrections

- **ID-JAG composition check.** The consolidated sentence said to include the `jwt-bearer` grant type "there", which reads as `authorization_grant_profiles_supported`. Section 7.2 of ID-JAG puts it in `grant_types_supported`.
- **Relationship Authentication.** The Retrieval Binding definition and the Applicability section point to this section, but it no longer mentioned Retrieval Bindings. Its opening sentence is restored, with a pointer to the Retrieval Binding paragraph in Extensibility.
- **Client assertion example.** The example used the same `kid` as the catalog access assertion, contradicting the SHOULD to use a different key. Its header now decodes to `{"alg":"ES256","kid":"client-key-1"}`.

## Pointers and terms

- The `sub_id` pointer now says "for an ID-JAG", because the JWT representation is now part of the ID-JAG profile.
- "Key binding" becomes "grant binding", the term used everywhere else.
- The ID-JAG grant binding text names the IdP Authorization Server as the party that binds the ID-JAG, as Section 9.11.1.1 of ID-JAG does. "It" had come to read as the client.
- "A catalog does not authorize any request" now points to the Introduction instead of Permitted Grants.
- External References cites both credential rules: `rar-metadata` for the metadata URIs, and `view-document` for the catalog access token.
- The client identifier sentence assigns the rule to the Grant Profile Definition, not the Grant Profile.

## Checks

- Builds at 62 pages.
- idnits: only template indentation warnings and the two draft downrefs.
- All references are cited and every citation resolves.

pulls.title: Restructure for a simple core with stated invariants
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Makes the spec easier to read by giving each rule one home and putting the core model in one place. No requirement changes. Each commit can be reviewed or dropped on its own.

## Commits

1. **Reorder sections for reading order** (moves only)
   - The Authorization Envelope now sits inside the Catalog Data Model, directly after the entry definitions.
   - Approval, issuance, and clients join Grant Issuer Processing, which now reads in lifecycle order: validate, compose, install, approve, issue, reconcile.
   - Identifier Uniqueness folds into the `id` convention, and Out of Scope into Applicability.

2. **One rule for the inputs that entry members govern**
   - Permitted-grant checks 4 to 8 become one rule plus a table (Table 3).
   - The commit message shows that the rule reproduces each former check. The only explicit exception kept is "a bound grant uses exactly one method".
   - The duplicated "if this member is absent" sentences become one pointer.

3. **Core Invariants section**
   - Nine invariants, right after the Protocol Overview: relationship scoping, whole views, closed world, one entry per grant, no logic in entries, narrowing only, public metadata prevails, revisions pin approvals, and safe extension.
   - It is a summary with pointers; each invariant is stated normatively where it is cited.
   - The must-understand open issue now asks whether extensions are to preserve these invariants.

4. **Member tables**
   - Each object is one table with columns member, status, and description.
   - `display` and `description` take one row per object instead of two entries.
   - Rules that sat inside member definitions move, unchanged, to prose under each table.

5. **Relationship View object in the data model**
   - The root object (`issuer`, `issuer_relationship`, `tenants`, `grant_catalogs`) is defined in the model, with a figure of the whole structure at the start of the section.
   - Validation checks 1 and 2 compare its members directly.
   - No wire change for the OAuth Retrieval Binding.

## Verification

- **Keyword counts:** MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, MAY, and REQUIRED counts are unchanged. OPTIONAL drops by 6, one per merged `display`/`description` pair.
- **Changed requirement sentences:** every BCP 14 sentence removed relative to main reappears with the same party, condition, and behavior. The changes are limited to:
  - "this member" becomes the member's name;
  - validation checks 1 to 3 compare the Relationship View's members (commit 5).
- **Newly leading sentences:** the two keyword sentences that now lead a paragraph were unconditional member rules before.
- **Prose:** rendered prose falls from 11,081 to 10,653 words, and from 126 to 121 words per keyword.
- **Build:** idnits shows only the template indentation warnings and the two draft downrefs.

**Pages:** the text rendering grows from 62 to 67 pages. xml2rfc does not split tables across pages in plain text, which leaves whitespace before each table. The HTML rendering is shorter. If the page count in the plain-text rendering matters more than scannability, commit 4 can be dropped on its own.

## Departure from the proposal

The object terms (Tenant Object, Grant Catalog, entry, Authorization Envelope) stay in Conventions and Definitions. The invariants come before the model and use those terms, so moving the definitions into the model would have left the invariants using terms not yet defined.

pulls.title: Separate client-facing discovery from Grant Issuer client views
pulls.author: mcguinness

pulls.title: Reorganize for an implementer's reading path
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This is an editorial restructure that follows the reading-path review. The wire format, the data model, and the behavior are unchanged. Each commit stands alone.

## Commits

1. **Implementation sequence (moves only)**
   - The sections now run: data model, then **Using a Catalog** (validate, check public metadata, approve, issue, install and reconcile, optional supporting metadata), then **Retrieving a Catalog**, then the ID-JAG profile, then Extensibility.
   - Grant Profile Definitions now sits under Extensibility.
   - Relationship Identity and Relationship Authorization move into Retrieving a Catalog. Its introduction says they apply to every retrieval protocol.
2. **Plain wording for two terms**
   - "Retrieval Binding" becomes "retrieval protocol".
   - "Catalog-Governed Input" becomes "input that an entry governs". Each of its uses was rewritten by hand so the protected resource stays covered.
   - Onboarding Arrangement and Grant Profile Definition are kept.
3. **One home for issuance rules**
   - Five Grant Issuer obligations move, unchanged, from the data model into Issuing a Grant, which now opens with the operative MUST. They come from the Authorization Envelope, Tenant Object, Claims, and Grant Binding sections.
   - Approval and Runtime Narrowing now cites Issuing a Grant to scope those rules to the approved subset.
4. **Transition table**
   - Installation and Policy Reconciliation merge into one section, with Table 16 as the rules for refresh and approval changes.
   - Each row carries the former rule verbatim. One new lowercase row says that changes outside an entry's normative semantics leave approvals in force.
   - The maximum-age SHOULD stays a separate sentence.
5. **Opening and example**
   - The Introduction has four paragraphs: problem, public-metadata gap, benefit, and boundary. The boundary is that a catalog does not establish trust, register clients, or grant access.
   - The motivating example is reduced to one tenant, `messages.read`, and DPoP, matching the example Relationship View in the data model.
   - The two-tenant approval case moves to Appendix B.
   - The metadata table now states the question each source answers.
6. **Invariants folded into the Overview**
   - Five principles at the end of the Protocol Overview replace the Core Invariants section. Each cites the section that states it.
   - Extensibility opens with a pointer to them. PR #4's commit message said this pointer existed, but it never reached the merged text.

## Verification

- **Sentence ledger** (comment below): 652 of 714 prose sentences on `main` appear verbatim. Each of the other 62 is accounted for:
  - 3 keyword sentences, now rows of Table 16;
  - 9 lowercase rules, moved or restated with the same outcome;
  - 17 rewritten narrative sentences;
  - 20 sentences of the folded invariants;
  - 3 removed definitions;
  - 10 redirected pointers and leads.
- **Keywords:** counts are identical once line wraps are removed: MAY 4, MUST 22, MUST NOT 35, OPTIONAL 24, REQUIRED 40, SHOULD 11, SHOULD NOT 1.
- **Other checks:**
  - Error-code mappings without a keyword: unchanged (2).
  - List items under a keyword lead: unchanged (25).
  - The three keyword sentences flagged as newly leading a paragraph already led their paragraphs on `main`. They were flagged only because the rename changed their wording.
- **Build:** 68 pages. idnits shows only the template indentation warnings and the two draft downrefs.

## Unresolved

The Tenant Object sentence "The data model has no defaults, inheritance, partial overrides, or merge rules" conflicts with the `optional` default for item requirements. It is unchanged here.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
## Sentence ledger

This ledger compares every prose sentence on `main` (8764b24) with this branch. Fenced blocks, headings, and table structure are excluded. The renames Retrieval Binding → retrieval protocol, `{{reconciliation}}` → `{{installation}}`, and `{{relationship-authentication}}` → its successors are neutralized before comparison.

Of 714 sentences, 652 appear verbatim. The 62 that do not are listed below by where they went.

### Requirement sentences (3): now rows of the transition table (Table 16), unchanged

| Sentence on main | Now |
| --- | --- |
| "…is withdrawn, and the Grant Issuer MUST stop issuing grants that depend on it in its previous form" | Withdrawal is defined in the first paragraph of Installation and Reconciliation. The MUST is the "withdrawn" row. |
| "The appearance of a new Tenant Object or entry MUST NOT, by itself, cause … and a change to an entry MUST NOT, by itself, expand an existing approval" | Two rows: "appears" and "an entry changes". Wording is verbatim. |

"Issuance resumes only after…" follows it in the same cell. |

- "State installed from an earlier retrieval remains in force, subject to the maximum age" is now the "incomplete" row.
- "The Grant Issuer obtains and validates a complete Relationship View, replaces the installed state…" is now the first paragraph of Installation and Reconciliation. "Reconciles its policy" is now the table.

pulls.title: Fix issues found in the cold read of the reading-path restructure
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #6. A cold review of the restructure found no behavior change, but it did find eleven text defects on main. All are fixed in one commit. BCP 14 keyword counts are unchanged.

## Requirement sentence

- **Issuing a Grant** opens with a MUST that referred to "the Tenant Object", which had no antecedent after the move. It now reads "the Tenant Object for which the grant is issued", which is what the sentence meant in its earlier place.

## Leftovers from the rename and the moves

- In Retrieving a Catalog, "the binding" and "This binding" now say "OAuth retrieval protocol" and "retrieval protocol". After the rename they read as grant binding.
- The target-tenant rule and the claim-release rule had merged into one paragraph. They are separate again.
- The second Overview principle now also cites Claims, which states the "reserved or listed" rule.
- Appendix B's "exactly one entry" now cites Issuing a Grant.

## Accuracy

- Extensibility now says the extension points are "designed to preserve" the principles. The old wording said they preserve them, which overstated the matter: the open issue asks whether to require that.
- The Introduction now says an administrator approves "a subset of each entry it uses", not a subset of the entries.
- The Motivating Example now gives the enterprise's tenant identifier at the application. The example Relationship View contains two tenant identifiers, so the old wording was ambiguous.

## Editorial

- Appendix B: the colon introduces the entries again, and the approval sentence follows the JSON.
- One double space removed.

pulls.title: Specify client discovery
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This PR specifies client discovery, the protected discovery mechanism that Section 9.7 of ID-JAG permits. Until now it was an open issue (#5). An application client retrieves the part of a catalog that applies to it, called a **client view**, and uses it to build its request to the Grant Issuer.

> Resource Authorization Servers MAY provide a protected discovery mechanism by which an authenticated client can determine whether an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant from a particular issuer would be accepted for that client. If such a mechanism is provided, the Resource Authorization Server MUST require client authentication before disclosing issuer-specific acceptance information. The response MUST be specific to the authenticated client and MAY also be scoped by tenant, resource, or other local policy context. (ID-JAG Section 9.7)

## Design

- **Endpoint:** a new Authorization Server Metadata member, `authorization_grant_client_discovery_endpoint`, registered with IANA.
- **Request:** a POST with these parameters:
  - `issuer`;
  - `issuer_tenant`;
  - `target_tenant`, REQUIRED when client identifiers are tenant-scoped (ID-JAG Section 6.2);
  - `resource`.

  The client authenticates with the method it uses at the token endpoint, as in introspection and PAR. Public clients cannot use the endpoint.
- **Disclosure authorization:** client authentication does not by itself authorize disclosure. Each of the following gets the same empty view, so the endpoint does not reveal which issuers and tenants the server trusts:
  - an unknown Grant Issuer;
  - an Issuer Relationship with no Onboarding Arrangement;
  - an unauthorized client;
  - a missing `issuer_tenant` for a multi-tenant Grant Issuer.
- **Client view:**
  - It is a Relationship View object plus `client_id`, served as `application/json` with `no-store`.
  - Its Tenant Objects and entries are identical to ones in the Relationship View for that Issuer Relationship. This keeps the revision identity rule intact. A narrower per-client configuration is published as a separate entry.
  - A Grant Issuer does not install a client view.
- **ID-JAG mapping:**
  - An entry maps to the Token Exchange request: `audience`, `resource`, `scope`, `authorization_details`, and DPoP or mTLS for binding.
  - The client neither requests claims nor selects `aud_tenant` (ID-JAG Section 6.4).

## Added requirements

| Requirement | Party | Who can observe a violation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MUST publish the endpoint metadata member | Resource Authorization Server | Any client |
| MUST authenticate the client; MUST NOT disclose to an unauthenticated client | Resource Authorization Server | Any caller |
| MUST NOT include a Tenant Object or entry the client is not authorized for | Resource Authorization Server | The Resource Authorization Server's auditor; not the client |
| MUST return the empty view for an unknown issuer, an unauthorized client, no Onboarding Arrangement, or a missing issuer tenant | Resource Authorization Server | A client comparing responses |
| Tenant Objects and entries MUST be identical to ones in the Relationship View | Resource Authorization Server | Only a party holding both views |
| MUST verify `issuer`, `issuer_relationship`, `client_id`, and the requested context; MUST NOT use a view that fails | Client | Not observable; a validation requirement |
| `invalid_client`, `invalid_request` per RFC 6749 Section 5.2 | Resource Authorization Server | The client |

No existing requirement is removed or reworded. Keyword counts on main were MUST 22, MUST NOT 35, REQUIRED 40, and OPTIONAL 24. They are now 28, 38, 43, and 27. The OPTIONAL and REQUIRED increases come from the new request parameters and `client_id`.

## Other edits

- Abstract, Applicability, and Overview (step F and the first principle).
- Clients.
- Grant Profile Definitions item 9.
- Security: a new Client Discovery subsection, and Protected Discovery now names this as the Section 9.7 mechanism.
- Privacy.
- IANA.
- Out of Scope: the client-discovery bullet is removed.
- Open Issues: the client-facing item is removed. The item on client-specific views retrieved by the Grant Issuer stays open.

Build: 73 pages. idnits reports only the template indentation warnings and the two draft downrefs.

A cold review from the client-implementer and Resource Authorization Server perspectives is still running. Its findings will be pushed to this PR.

pulls.title: Narrow the no-defaults sentence and fix the token endpoint assertion audience
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Resolves the two remaining small items.

## Tenant Object: "no defaults"

The sentence "The data model has no defaults, inheritance, partial overrides, or merge rules" conflicted with the `optional` default for an absent item requirement. It now says what it meant:

> A Tenant Object has no default Grant Catalog, and Grant Catalogs have no inheritance, partial overrides, or merge rules.

## Catalog access token request: client assertion audience

The draft did not say which audience a Grant Issuer's JWT client assertion carries at the token endpoint. It now matches the rule that #8 added for client discovery, and draft-ietf-oauth-rfc7523bis, which is in the RFC Editor queue:

> A Grant Issuer that authenticates with a JWT client assertion MUST use the issuer identifier of the Resource Authorization Server as the sole value of the assertion's `aud` claim, and the Resource Authorization Server MUST reject a client assertion that does not contain its issuer identifier as the sole audience value.

These two MUSTs are the only new requirements. The build is clean.

pulls.title: Fresh review, consolidation, and polish
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
A full pass in three phases. Each commit can be reviewed on its own.

## 1. Fresh review (55fe287)

Three cold reviewers read the whole draft: a working-group document reviewer, a security reviewer, and an implementer of both servers. None found a high-severity flaw. The findings below were verified against the text and the cached dependencies before being applied.

**Contradictions and terms**
- Extensibility no longer offers paging or delta retrieval, which contradicted complete views.
- When a revision changes back to an approved value, issuance resumes under an approval made for that value. The transition table and the Overview now say so.
- "Grant Catalog" no longer stands for the whole catalog.
- The Issuer Relationship is now the relationship itself, not a pair of identifiers.
- "client", "issuer tenant", and "target tenant" are defined.
- A catalog access assertion is not a "grant" in this specification's sense.
- Issuing a Grant lists when an entry is usable with a Tenant Object.
- Envelope rule 4 has one clause per requirement level.

**Security**
- New subsection, Tenant Eligibility (SHOULD): a tenant is made eligible only with agreement on the Grant Issuer side, and administrators identify a Tenant Object by `target_tenant`, not by `display`.
- Client discovery: registering a client does not authorize disclosure.
- The token-endpoint audience MUST is scoped to catalog requests. Before, it bound every client at the endpoint.
- Refresh tokens change from SHOULD NOT to MUST NOT. An existing MUST already made them unusable.
- The `jti` check and its recording are atomic.
- The catalog endpoint verifies DPoP proofs and rejects a DPoP-bound token sent as a bearer token (RFC 9449 Section 7.2).
- A Grant Issuer treats a Relationship View response with any other media type as an incomplete retrieval.
- Stale Catalogs no longer claims that the maximum age is enforceable.

**Implementation**
- Composition runs when a Relationship View is installed. No response to the Protected Resource Metadata request is treated like a response other than 200.
- `null` has no specified type.
- The `scope` parameter is exactly `authorization_grant_catalog.read`.
- A counter or a digest satisfies the revision uniqueness rule.
- The DPoP-proof note in the ID-JAG profile says a request with a valid proof cannot use an entry that permits no usable binding method.

**References**
- RFC 9700 and RFC7523BIS move to normative.
- OpenID.Core is added.
- A citation of RFC 6749 Section 3.3 that did not support the claim is removed.

**Examples**
- `tenant-123` references the `read-only` catalog everywhere.
- The ID-JAG example uses `tenant-456`.
- The metadata example lists the client discovery endpoint.

**Not adopted**
- Lowering producer-side MUSTs that a Grant Issuer cannot verify, such as Tenant Object identifier reuse and "one consistent state". These are normal producer obligations.
- Relaxing all-or-nothing validation. It is deliberate.
- Requiring a shared `jti` record across endpoints. RFC 7523 makes `jti` optional.

## 2. Consolidation and polish (525d845, 7371a51)

Six section editors worked from frozen rules, in two waves. The body went first; Security, Privacy, IANA, and the appendices followed against the settled body.

- 65 edits were proposed. 57 were applied, one of them adjusted, and 8 were declined.
- The editors removed restatement, replaced restated dependency text with citations, and fixed grammar, pronoun, and long-sentence problems.
- Security and Privacy subsections are now the threat, a pointer to the mitigating rule, and the residual risk.
- The declined edits would have cut content kept on purpose:
  - the client discovery mapping to the three requirements of ID-JAG Section 9.7;
  - the `aud_tenant` and `sub_id` cross-links;
  - "every claim is reserved or listed";
  - the note on overlapping transition-table rows;
  - the reason the DPoP proof is validated before the assertion's `jti` is consumed.

## 3. Verification (e2ff552)

**Obligation verifier: no normative change.** It checked all 157 BCP 14 sentences, with the context that carries their conditions, and all 71 sentences rewritten during consolidation. The ordered keyword sequence is identical across the consolidation commits.

**Consistency reader:** 14 seam fixes. The main ones:
- Appendix C used `tenant-123` with the `standard` catalog.
- The view document example pointed at a figure that belongs to a different Issuer Relationship.
- Grant Profile Definitions item 10 is added: how the Grant Issuer obtains the client identifier. Clients already promised it.
- A 304 response counts as a complete retrieval.
- Relationship Authorization lists eligible tenants among what an Onboarding Arrangement records.

## Net

- **Keywords relative to main:** SHOULD +1; SHOULD NOT −1 and MUST NOT +1 (refresh tokens). Everything else is unchanged.
- **Length:** prose is 1.6% longer (12,964 → 13,170 words, 75 → 77 pages), because the review fixes added more text than consolidation removed.
- **Build:** idnits reports only template indentation warnings and the two draft downrefs.

## Open decision

How long a Grant Issuer may keep issuing after a relationship ends. The bound is currently the Grant Issuer's own maximum age, which is a SHOULD. The options are:
- make it a MUST;
- have the Resource Authorization Server publish an upper bound;
- keep the documented procedure: empty the view, wait, then end the relationship.

This PR keeps the procedure.

pulls.title: Narrow -00: defer client discovery and supporting-metadata detail
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This PR applies a scope review: -00 now focuses on the catalog between the Grant Issuer and the Resource Authorization Server. The core data model, the approval lifecycle, and the security rules are unchanged.

## Deferred

- **Client discovery** (#8) is removed. This covers:
  - the endpoint and request;
  - the disclosure rules and the client view;
  - client processing;
  - the ID-JAG request mapping;
  - the Security subsection and the IANA entry.

  Open Issues now describes the considered design and its known limit: a client view selects whole entries, so it cannot express a restriction for one client that is narrower than an entry, and the Grant Issuer can issue a grant using a different entry from the one the client used. The Out of Scope bullet for client discovery is restored. ID-JAG Section 9.7 makes this mechanism optional.
- **Optional Supporting Metadata** is reduced to a short note:
  - such metadata is advisory;
  - it cannot broaden an entry or an approval;
  - its absence does not affect the validity of an entry.

  The credential MUST NOT stays. Schema retention, authority-entry matching, and runtime attenuation move to a new open issue.

## Reading path

- **Overview:** one concrete sentence on how the OAuth retrieval protocol works: sign a catalog access assertion, exchange it for a catalog access token, and retrieve one complete Relationship View. This is kept separate from the client's grant flow.
- **Data model:** how the Relationship View, Tenant Objects, and Grant Catalogs relate, and that each approval is specific to one Tenant Object.
- **Motivating Example:** what the catalog replaces and what it does not, now including subject mapping. Approving an entry constrains what grants contain. What a scope value permits, and runtime access decisions, stay with the application.

## Other

- **Open Issues:** freshness and relationship termination. The Resource Authorization Server has no deadline it can rely on, because the maximum age is configured by the Grant Issuer and is a SHOULD. This records the open decision for -00 feedback instead of adding a mechanism.
- **Entry Revision:** the revision is now described as opaque, with no integrity guarantee. The previous text said it was "neither a digest", which conflicted with allowing a digest as its value.
- **Grant Profile Definitions checklist:** stays in Extensibility, without the client discovery item, and now has nine items.

## Checks

- **Requirements removed:**
  - the client discovery rules: 10 keyword sentences and 3 error mappings;
  - two MAYs about using supporting metadata.

  No other requirement changes.
- **References:** no references to removed anchors remain, and all citations resolve. OpenID.Core is dropped because nothing cites it any longer.
- **Size:** 77 pages before, 71 after.

pulls.title: Link each open issue to its GitHub issue
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This PR links each item in the Open Issues appendix to the GitHub issue that tracks it (#12 to #20). Each item ends with "Tracked as issue #N" and a link.

It also marks the Open Issues and Document History appendices for removal before publication ("RFC Editor: please remove this appendix before publication").

The repository and its issue tracker are already linked from the "About This Document" note, which the `venue` front matter generates. No front-matter key exists for individual issues, so these per-item links are inline. The `open-issue` label on the GitHub issues lists them all in the tracker.

No requirement changes. The build is clean.

pulls.title: Limit Protected Resource Metadata requests to https resources; align the reapproval issue
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
This PR fixes two findings from a full review of the reduced draft.

## Composition with non-https resources (P2)

An entry's `resource` can be any absolute URI without a fragment (RFC 8707 Section 2), for example `urn:example:messages`. However, Protected Resource Metadata resource identifiers are https URLs (RFC 9728 Section 1.2):

> The protected resource's resource identifier, which is a URL that uses the https scheme and has no fragment component.

Composition step 2 requested metadata unconditionally, so implementations could disagree about whether such an entry fails composition or simply has no metadata. The step now:
- requests metadata only for an https `resource`, using the `oauth-protected-resource` well-known suffix (RFC 9728 Section 3);
- otherwise has no effect, which matches how the draft treats unavailable metadata.

## Reapproval open issue (P3)

The issue said every revision change suspends issuance until reapproval. The transition table, however, lets an earlier approval apply again when its revision returns. The issue now describes a change to a revision "for which no approval already applies".

No requirement keywords change. The build is clean.

pulls.title: Tighten the Open Issues appendix
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Each open issue now states its question in one or two sentences, keeps its pointers to the relevant sections, and links to its GitHub issue. The appendix drops from about 750 words to 370.

The fuller descriptions and history stay in the tracker. Issues #12 to #20 quote the previous, longer text. For example, #15 records the client discovery design, and #16 records the freshness options.

No requirement changes. The build is clean.

pulls.title: Keep only the key open issues in the document
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
The Open Issues appendix now lists only the questions that change the core design and that working-group feedback should address.

**Kept in the document**
- Reapproval (#12): the main operational trade-off of the approval lifecycle.
- Client-facing discovery (#15): the mechanism that ID-JAG Section 9.7 invites, deliberately deferred.
- Freshness and termination (#16): the Resource Authorization Server has no enforceable deadline after a relationship ends.
- Must-understand extensions (#19): needed before restrictive extensions can be defined safely.

**Tracker only**

These issues stay open on GitHub. The "About This Document" note links the tracker.
- Token path (#13)
- Client-specific views for the Grant Issuer (#14)
- Supporting metadata (#17)
- Registries (#18)
- Implementation experience (#20)

**Body sentences changed**

Four sentences called these issues open. They now say what this document does not define, so no pointer refers to a removed item:
- Clients
- Optional Supporting Metadata
- Catalog Access Token Response
- the "No client inventory" rationale

The appendix drops to about 200 words, and the draft drops from 71 to 69 pages. No requirement changes. The build is clean.

pulls.title: Name the Relationship View's server members by role
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
The Relationship View had a top-level `issuer` for the Resource Authorization Server and a nested `issuer_relationship.issuer` for the Grant Issuer. Two members called `issuer` named two different servers.

## Rename

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `issuer` (Relationship View and each Grant Catalog) | `authorization_server` |
| `issuer_relationship` | `grant_issuer` |

- `authorization_server` follows the RFC 9728 `authorization_servers` pattern, in which a role name holds an issuer identifier. In a Grant Catalog it is the audience of grants issued using the catalog.
- `grant_issuer` still identifies the Issuer Relationship. Its `issuer` and `tenant` members are unchanged.

```json
{
  "authorization_server": "https://ras.example/",
  "grant_issuer": { "issuer": "https://idp.example/", "tenant": "org-acme" },
  "tenants": [ ... ],
  "grant_catalogs": [ { "authorization_server": "https://ras.example/", "id": "read-only", "entries": [ ... ] } ]
}
```

## Updated

- the Relationship View and Grant Catalog member tables
- the structure figure
- every catalog JSON example
- validation checks 1 and 2
- envelope rule 1
- composition step 1
- the list of members that carry protocol values

The Authorization Server Metadata example keeps its RFC 8414 `issuer`.

No behavior changes. All eight complete JSON examples parse, and the build is clean.

pulls.title: Align three explanations with the rules they describe
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Three editorial corrections from a pre-publication review. The reviewer found no protocol blocker and recommends publishing -00 with the current scope.

- **Revision Integrity and Approval:**
  - "new approval for every revision change" becomes "an approval for the installed revision". This matches the transition table, under which an earlier approval applies again when its revision returns.
  - "expand authorization" becomes "expand the approved subset", which keeps it distinct from the runtime authorization decision.
- **Design Rationale:** "Revision rather than digest" becomes "Opaque revision identifiers". Entry Revision allows a digest of the normative semantics, so the rationale now says that the format leaves revision generation to the publisher and prescribes no canonicalization.
- **Relationship Authorization and Assertion Trust:** the shared-key risk is now stated conditionally. When a Resource Authorization Server accepts one signing key for several Issuer Relationships, compromise of that key exposes their catalogs. The protocol requires no particular key arrangement.

No requirement changes. The build is clean.

pulls.title: Simplify the Relationship View: one authorization server, tenant_id
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Two data model simplifications before -00. No behavior change other than the members removed below.

## 1. State the authorization server once (5eddd5c)

Each Grant Catalog repeated the Relationship View's `authorization_server`. All catalogs arrive together in one complete Relationship View and must name the same server, so the copy carried no information and could disagree with the view.

- The member is removed from Grant Catalogs.
- Envelope rule 1: the audience is now the `authorization_server` of the Relationship View that contains the Grant Catalog.
- Validation check 1 and composition step 1 compare the Relationship View's `authorization_server`.
- Appendices A and B show standalone catalogs, so their text now names the authorization server.

## 2. Identify a Tenant Object by its tenant identifier (8edc88b)

A Tenant Object had an `id` and a `target_tenant`. The separate `id` let a Tenant Object survive a change to its tenant identifier, but such a change already suspended approvals. It also needed a rule forbidding derivation of the target tenant from the `id`.

```json
{ "tenant_id": "customer-acme", "display": "Acme", "grant_catalog": "read-only" }
```

- `tenant_id` is the exact Resource Authorization Server tenant identifier that a grant conveys as its target tenant (`aud_tenant` for ID-JAG). It is omitted only when the server's issuer identifier alone identifies the tenant. Values are unique, and at most one Tenant Object omits it.
- A different `tenant_id` is a different Tenant Object. The old one is withdrawn, and the new one needs approval.
- Approvals retain the `tenant_id`. The transition table and the Overview principle no longer list `target_tenant` changes separately.

## Requirements removed

- the REQUIRED `authorization_server` member of each Grant Catalog;
- the REQUIRED `id` member of each Tenant Object;
- the MUST NOT on reusing a Tenant Object `id` for a different tenant (tenant identifiers are not reassigned, by definition);
- the Tenant Object `id` clause of the target-tenant derivation MUST NOT.

## Checks

All eight JSON examples parse, and the build is clean.

pulls.title: Final polish before -00
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Final pass before submitting -00. There are three commits and no requirement changes. The ordered BCP 14 keyword sequence is identical, with 135 keywords.

1. **Pin the OpenID Enterprise Extensions reference** to the draft-01 URL. The unversioned URL changes when a new draft posts. (18242b1)
2. **Final tightening** (99a8ec7). Two section editors proposed 40 edits under frozen rules; 33 are applied.
   - The applied edits remove restatement and padding and clean up wording left by the renames (`authorization_server`, `grant_issuer`, `tenant_id`) and by the removal of client discovery.
   - The declined edits would have cut content kept on purpose:
     - the sentence separating catalog retrieval from the client's grant flow;
     - the approval reminder in the data model example;
     - the `aud_tenant` and `sub_id` cross-links;
     - "every claim is reserved or listed";
     - the note on overlapping transition-table rows;
     - "end user" in place of the OpenID Connect term "End-User".
   - Formatting fixes: token request step 6 indentation, the metadata example indentation, and extra blank lines.
3. **Motivation, from an adoption review** (fb6cc9f).
   - The Introduction says that deployments communicate grant requirements through documentation or implementation-specific configuration. The catalog is a common, authenticated representation that a Resource Authorization Server publishes and a Grant Issuer uses to configure issuance and detect changes.
   - The Introduction says that a grant constructed from an entry can still be rejected. The catalog states how to construct a grant that avoids preventable failures, not whether a request will succeed.
   - The Motivating Example says what becomes detectable: a new revision stops issuance until review, and a removed tenant stops issuance for that tenant.

## Pre-submission gates on this branch

- `make lint` is clean.
- `make next` builds `draft-mcguinness-oauth-grant-catalog-00`: 68 pages, no lines over 72 columns, no xml2rfc warnings.
- `make idnits` reports no errors. It reports 3 expected warnings for normative references to drafts (ID-JAG, JWT-DPOP, RFC7523BIS). It reports 3 comments: the external normative reference to OpenID.Enterprise, a no-break space in the standard BCP 14 boilerplate, and `<?line?>` processing instructions.

A fresh pre-publication read of the candidate -00 is running. Any findings will be pushed to this PR.

pulls.title: Fix the final pre-publication findings
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Fixes from the final read of the candidate -00, which found two blockers. No requirement changes; the only edit to a requirement sentence adds a citation to the `schema_uri` MUST NOT.

## Blockers

- **"Accepts" contradiction.** The Introduction said that the Resource Authorization Server "rejects any other grant", and the empty-`entries` rule said it "accepts no grants". Security Considerations, by contrast, says a catalog does not list every grant the server accepts. The Introduction sentence is removed, and the empty-`entries` rule and the metadata table now say "offers".
- **Broken pointer.** A Design Rationale sentence cited Optional Supporting Metadata for how entries align with authority metadata. That detail was cut in #11, so the pointer is removed.

## Also

- The `id` length limit now applies to the Grant Catalog and entry identifiers retained with an approval. `tenant_id` has no limit.
- `schema_uri` now cites RAR-METADATA, which defines it.
- The metadata example no longer includes the authorization details types metadata endpoint, which no text uses after #11.
- The ID-JAG `typ` sentence no longer reads "Section 9.11" as an ID-JAG section.
- The view document example now says that it is a different Issuer Relationship (issuer tenant `acme-workforce`) from the data model example.

Not changed: the review suggested also changing the data model example's issuer tenant to `acme-workforce`. Both examples are complete views, so that would give one Issuer Relationship two views that disagree.

## Checks

- **Build:** clean at 68 pages.
- **JSON:** all eight examples parse.
- **`make next`:** no line exceeds 72 columns.
- **`make idnits`:** only the expected warnings for normative references to drafts, and the template comments.

pulls.title: Editorial restructuring: shorter paragraphs and bulleted requirements
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Editorial pass toward -01. It splits dense paragraphs, presents lists of requirements and conditions as bullets, and simplifies wording. No requirement changes.

## Changes

- Four section editors worked from frozen rules. They proposed 78 edits, and all 78 were reviewed and applied.
- Dense paragraphs are split by topic.
- Inline lists of three or more parallel items become bullets. Examples:
  - values typed by hand;
  - what stays outside the catalog;
  - what an approval retains;
  - what an Onboarding Arrangement records;
  - the `invalid_grant` conditions.
- Paragraphs that state several requirements on one party become bulleted lists. Each item keeps its own BCP 14 keyword, so no keyword is merged under a shared lead. Examples:
  - the `tenant_id` rules;
  - the revision MUST and MUST NOT;
  - Relationship Identity;
  - the token response.
- Complete and incomplete retrieval are now a short definition list.
- Document History gets a -01 entry.

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraphs over 80 words | 28 | 1 |
| Average sentence length | 20.9 words | 18.0 words |
| 90th-percentile sentence length | 37 words | 31 words |
| Rendered prose | 11,011 words | 10,896 words |
| Pages | 68 | 75 (bullets take more vertical space) |

## Verification

- **Keyword counts:** unchanged once line wraps are removed (MUST 24, MUST NOT 35, SHOULD 12, MAY 2, REQUIRED 38, OPTIONAL 24).
- **Unchanged content:** no fenced block or anchor changed. All eight JSON examples parse. Every numbered list that other text cites keeps its numbering.
- **Obligation verifier:**
  - It checked all 135 recorded BCP 14 sentences, every lowercase rule, every error-code mapping, and every reason.
  - It found one problem. The "In that case" lead made all four client-assertion rules conditional on required client authentication, although two of them had no such condition. Fixed in the second commit.
- **Rendering:** all 137 bullets render as lists, including the lists nested inside numbered items and definitions.
